text: HCM City approves central square and administrative center project

The Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee has approved the Central City Square and Administrative Center Project to be implemented under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, using a Build-Transfer (BT) contract, with a total investment estimated at nearly VND30 trillion ($1.165 billion).
The project will be developed in An Khanh Ward and requires approximately 47 ha of land, comprising four component projects.

According to the master plan, the landscaped park area will cover more than 33 ha, including a 50,000-sq.m underground parking facility, approximately 22 ha of parkland, and various supporting facilities.

The project also includes the upgrading and expansion of a 1.13-km section of To Huu Street within the planning area, as well as the construction of parallel frontage roads along Mai Chi Tho Boulevard (640 m) and Nguyen Co Thach Street (540 m).

The City Administrative Center will feature two basement levels and 30 above-ground floors, reaching a height of nearly 170 m. The construction site will cover more than 78,300 sq.m, with a total gross floor area of approximately 389,100 sq.m.
The Convention and Performing Arts Center is designed to accommodate around 2,000 seats.
The Central City Square will occupy 119,000 sq.m and is expected to host approximately 268,000 people during major political events and up to 500,000 people during cultural festivals.
According to the city government, the complex is envisioned as a modern, centralized administrative hub that will help address the current dispersion of government offices.
The project will also create additional green spaces and public areas while meeting the demand for large-scale events, festivals, and community activities.
Sai Gon Sun Investment and Development Co., Ltd. has been selected as the project investor.

The implementation phase is expected to take place during 2026-2027, covering detailed design and cost estimate appraisal, contractor selection, construction, supervision, acceptance testing, and handover of the completed facilities for operation.
